reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling publishes 24 MW of IT capacity in a 154,230-square-foot facility, ranking 17th among Virginia's 25 data centers with disclosed power figures and accounting for 1.5% of the state's announced 1,603 MW total.

At the common 40 kW-per-rack density used for AI training, this translates to roughly 600 racks. The facility's position reflects Virginia's broader pattern: 330 data centers exist in the state but only 25 publish power specifications. Most of the ecosystem remains opaque to capacity planning.

Whether Sterling matters for AI scaling cannot be determined from published information. The operator has not disclosed whether it accepts high-density compute, whether power delivery can scale beyond the current 24 MW, or how much grid headroom Northern Virginia has to support it. The absence of certifications is consistent with many regional facilities but leaves fundamental questions about capability unanswered.
